articles.text: On November 16, Shell Oil issued a press release inviting Piedmont residents to a community meeting to be held on November 16 to inform community members of the conversion of the former Piedmont Auto Care to Shell Recharge, a recharging station for electric vehicles. Equilon Enterprises LLC d/b/a Shell Oil Products U.S. (Shell), a subsidiary of Shell plc, is excited to announce it has acquired a piece of property at 29 Wildwood Ave., in Piedmont, California. This is currently the site of a former gas station previously owned by Piedmont Auto Care. Pending permitting and regulatory approvals, Shell hopes to construct a new, 14-bay electric vehicle (EV) charging hub at the site under the Shell Recharge brand. Shell envisions this site to be part of our growing state and national network of fast charging for electric vehicles. A robust electric vehicle charging network can play a role in California’s plans to achieve 100% of new zero-emission vehicle sales by 2035, and to achieve 25% reduction in smog causing pollution by 2037. Once constructed, the proposed electric vehicle hub at this site in Piedmont would provide fast charging for electric vehicles with power up to 360kW, allowing drivers to recharge most vehicles more quickly, getting them back on the road faster. This location will be owned and operated by Shell. Construction is expected to commence in the first half of 2024. During demolition of the existing infrastructure, and installation of new equipment, you may notice additional traffic, workers on site, and normal construction noise. Shell is committed to being a good neighbor and has a process in place to receive feedback as we build the hub. You can reach us with concerns or feedback by calling 1-888-GO-SHELL (888- 467-4355). Please be sure to refer to the location at 29 Wildwood in Piedmont, California. Also, to learn more about this Piedmont location and Shell e-Mobility, please join us at our open house at Kehilla Community Synagogue, 1300 Grand Avenue, Piedmont on Tuesday, November 28, 2023, from 4:00- 6:00 p.m. We look forward to hosting you and supporting Piedmont’s charging needs. If you have any questions, please contact us at 1-888-GO-SHELL (888-467-4355). Sincerely, Shell Recharge Team Customers of Piedmont Auto Care owned by Jeff Hansen for the past 17 years learned in a news story in the Piedmont Post on November 8 that the station had been sold to Shell Oil and that the gas station had closed. The Piedmont Shell Station has closed after 95 years in business.

Some delays in the project have been caused by the City’s requirement to use fiber technology instead of wireless technology. articles.text: Piedmont Scout Council’s annual Tree Lot will open this Saturday, November 25, at 9 a.m. The lot is located at Coaches Field, next to the Corporation Yard on Moraga Avenue. Community members looking to add a festive touch to their homes this holiday season will be able to buy trees, wreaths, garlands, tree stands, and mistletoe from the lot for pickup or delivery. The Tree Lot is also currently accepting online pre-orders at www.scouttreelot.org. Delivery of trees will be available throughout Piedmont and select neighborhoods in Oakland. Proceeds from the lot benefit local Cub Scouts, Scouts, Venturers, Explorers, and the Piedmont Language School. “It’s fun because you get to interact with everyone from Piedmont,” said Kevin McKillop, a Troop 6 Scout. “It’s especially fun when we deliver because people are always super happy to receive their trees.” In recent years, the tree lot has become something of a family affair for Kevin. For the last six years, Kevin has volunteered at the tree lot with his father, Sean McKillop, the Scoutmaster for Sunday Photos by Tom Smegal Volunteer Scouts and parents plan for opening day of the Piedmont Scout Tree Lott, scheduled for this Saturday, November 25. Troop 6. “Mostly we try to volunteer together,” explained Kevin. “But, if one of us has something going on at school or at work, we’ll still go separately.” This year, the father-son duo is assisting with set-up, breakdown, and deliveries for the tree lot. Kevin said that even as a teenager, volunteering at the tree lot still holds its appeal. “As a teenager, you’re kind of hesitant to say yes at first because you have other stuff you want to do during the holiday season. But, once you get there, you have more fun. It’s just a good time.” As with everything related to the tree lot, family remains central to the volunteer staff as well. Sean McKillop said that volunteering with the tree lot was a great way to spend time with his son. “To be honest with you, Kevin is going away to college next year, so any opportunity I get to spend time with him is a bonus,” he said. The Scout Tree Lot has been highly successful in previous years. In 2022, sales were high with up to $50,000 generated on its opening weekend, and an additional $30,000 in online sales. articles.text: Donation bins will remain out until December 23 The Piedmont Fire Department is currently accepting donations for its annual toy drive through December 23. To ensure that kids everywhere have a present to open for Christmas, Piedmont residents are encouraged to donate new, unwrapped toys to the Fire Department’s annual Toys for Tots Drive. Donation bins are located at the Fire Station and City Hall on Vista Avenue. . You’re never too old to donate, nor too young, as the fire department found out. This week, children from Havens Elementary School’s Minimates walked across the street to the fire station for a photograph in the Post, each holding a donation to the toy drive. The toy drive brings back some fond memories to Piedmont firefighters, “I grew up in a very large family,” said Fire Engineer Anthony Renteria. “I have a lot of younger brothers and sisters. So being able to help out kids in the area really hits home for me.” Firefighter Nadder Shehadeh echoed the sentiment. “Like, certain toys that you see go in these bins, you’re like, ‘Wow, I remember playing with this as a kid.’ Hopefully, these toys bring joy to someone’s day and bring light to their nights this holiday season.” “Seeing some of these toys come in just brings back old memories,” added Shehadeh, smiling. In particular, he said someone’s donated etch-a-sketch reminded him of his own memories of playing with it as a child. “I didn’t know they still made them.” Donated toys will be distributed to families in Oakland and Alameda County, and any toys donated before December 8 will be distributed through the US Marine Corps Reserve’s Toys for Tots Foundation. Toys donated on or after December 8 will be distributed at the annual Three Wise Men toy giveaway in Oakland’s Fruitvale neighborhood. Bins will remain at the F ire Department and City Hall for donations through December 23. A child donates the classic board game Jenga to the toy drive. articles.text: The Piedmont Junior Running Club held its inaugural race in Dracena Park on November 15. Conditions were ideal as the rain forecasted for that day never materialized. A total of 64 runners from 4th and 5th grades in all three Piedmont elementary schools participated in the 0.9- mile event. The runners navigated the paved path that winds through the park, including uphill and downhill segments and challenging curves. The event was staged in three heats, each comprising about 20 participants. Every runner received a medal for finishing, and individual trophies were awarded to the top three boys and three girls in each heat. The heat winners were: Heat 1: Will Brumfiel (Wildwood), Cate Brasfield (Havens) Heat 2: Timmy Edit (Havens), Lanea Patty (Beach) Heat 3: Max Centeno (Wildwood), Harper Maing (Beach) Max Centeno posted the fastest overall time for the day, finishing the course in 6 minutes, 18 seconds, and Harper Maing was the fastest girl in 6 minutes and 46 seconds. Piedmont Middle School’s sixth graders concluded their studies of the ancient Egyptians with a Festival of the Nile on Thursday, November 16. Each 6th grade class performed a skit to show the mastery of ancient Egyptian social structures, religious beliefs and culture. Stories detailing the beliefs and practices were transformed into contemporary song and dance on stage. Performances described the social hierarchy of the civilization and the 4400-year-old pyramids of Giza. PMS students even learned the ways of mummification in recent Photos by Jay Russell and Anne Smith Ava Ubaka is dressed as a pharaoh. Felix Kansal with a headdress and “gold” around his neck played a dead pharaoh. Mireille Psathas is costumed as Isis, the Ancient Egyptian Goddess of healing and magic. Students in Michael Bracamonte’s 6th grade core class fly through the air in dramatic choreography Posters made by each sixth grade class depict mythological stories from Ancient Egypt. The comic item shows how Seth betrayed his brother, Osiris. weeks. The high priests removed and jarred a dead Pharoah’s organs except for the heart, which was to be weighed against a feather by Anubis before entering the afterworld. Hillary Voigt’s class did a fun version of Michael Jackson’s “Thriller.” Class performances had different strengths. Caroline Woods’ class, as example, made fantastic stage props that required hours of work to create a makeshift sarcophagus from paper and cardboard. Lea Lotia’s afternoon core class was light on dress up, but big on the recitation of a song and a choreographed story. Michael Bracamonte’s class staged an elaborate skit portraying the beliefs of the Egyptian afterlife. “Where am I, who are you?” asked a student portraying a dead Pharaoh. “I’m Anubis and you are dead. Remember you’re in the land of the dead now; you have no power here,” said the student wearing the head of a jackal. In its second year as an annual event for sixth graders, the Festival of the Nile has quickly become an enjoyable way for students to showcase their history lessons.

articles.text: Piedmont’s boys’ water polo team’s illustrious season came to an end in the first round of the Division 3 CIF NorCal Championship Tournament, in a close 10-8 loss to No. 4 Ponderosa in Elk Grove. The Highlanders finished with a 19-10 record and won the school’s first North Coast Section championship. The team will lose the bulk of its roster to graduation at the end of the school year. Seniors include Peter Krumins. Declan Linnane, George Stein, Quincy Scherman, Finn Burke, Daniel Banin, Spencer Barlow, and Evan Dickason. Next year ‘s team will have returners that include goalie Luke McAuliffe, starters Elles Krieckhaus and Leo Hurwitz, in addition to Charlie Wright, Yotam Kariv, and Ori Aloush. Coach Rik Krumins is also keeping a watchful eye on some of next year’s freshmen arrivals. “We’re hoping this championship season helps build the next 10 years of this program. That’s the excitement we have. There’s a really good class coming in next year, and I’m really excited to be a part of it,” said Krumins. Game Recap Piedmont trailed 3-2 by the end of the first quarter and faced a 6-3 deficit by halftime. Piedmont closed the score to 7-6 at the start of the fourth quarter, but conceded three goals while being held to Staff Photos George Stein scored three goals in his final appearance in a Piedmont cap. Piedmont’s Elles Kreickhaus will likely be among the headline returners in 2024. Declan Linnane scored once against Ponderosa.

Piedmont High’s cross-country team competed in the North Coast Section Championship at Hayward High on Saturday, November 18. The girls’ team finished sixth of 16 schools, and the boys’ team was eighth of 19. It was a wet and stormy day for the event with scattered downpours soaking the course. The big news was freshman Sebastien Swain qualifying for the CIF State Meet by placing 13th of 140 runners with a time of 16:29.5. Individual runners could qualify by finishing among the five fastest runners not on a topthree team. It has been a breakout season for Swain, who helped pace his team late in the season. “By Mile 2, Sebastien in 20th and continued to work his way up, passing other runners to finish in 13th place. Sebastian’s poise, determination and good racing aptitude allowed him to rise to the occasion,” said PHS coach Steve Zirkelbach. The boys’ team was hampered by senior leader Xander Schulte-Sasse dealing with a lingering injury. Tanya Kononova completed her Piedmont High tennis career on Monday and Tuesday, November 13-14 at the Division 2 North Coast Section Individual Tournament. She finished 3rd in the singles bracket, defeating Noelle Chen of Head-Royce in straight sets, 7-5, 6-1. In the first round, Kononova defeated Iris Bremer of Arcata 6-3, 6-3 and followed up with a 6-2, 6-3 win over Marin Academy’s Eloise Sent. She then ran into the No.1 seed and eventual-champion Vivian Gallaway of Berean Christian in the semifinals, losing 6-1, 6-3. “After playing Vivian, I was really down. Jim [Landes] reminded me it’s my last match. I started playing my game and it felt really good. I just had to get myself all together,” said Kononova. After a narrow first-set win over Chen, Kononova powered her way to the finish in the second set. She showed her usual array of forehands, but also used approaches to net to keep Chen off balance. It marked the second time Kononova faced Chen this season. The Jayhawks’ starter won the first meeting in a narrow 7-5, 7-6 (7-5) straight sets victory. articles.text: Piedmont’s boys’ basketball team opens its season this Saturday afternoon, November 25, with a 2 p.m. game with Analy at Binks Rawlings Gym. After reaching the semifinals of the North Coast Section post-season playoffs, the Highlanders are hungry for more success. “In the years before, we talked about defense being the thing we needed to improve on, like not being able to stop Branson’s guards. That’s been the big push this offseason. We’ve had more offseason workouts than ever,” said coach Ben Spencer. The Highlanders will have to operate without last year’s leading scorer, A.J. Harris, now playing at Emory University. Leading the team group will be a tall, versatile center, Brit Burden, who Spencer compared to Luke Barrett in 2020. “He looks great. He can also play away from the basket, stretch the floor, but also play with his back to the basket,” said Spencer. Tall and lanky is a good way to describe this year’s roster. Declan Linnane is fresh off a highly successful water polo season and will provide a big body to grab boards and play tough defense. Center Scott Cooley, listed at 6 feet, 6 inches, is still working on clearance from section officials. From top to bottom, it’s a tall team. “This is the biggest team we’ve had,” said Spencer. “This year, Brit is 6’6”. Scott Cooley is a new transfer student and he’s 6’6”. Declan is 6’4”, Alex Anderson is 6’3”,” he said. Alongside Burden will be returning guards junior Ravi Silverberg and senior point guard Arjun Bornstein. Piedmont’s boys’ basketball team gets its season started this week, so we are taking a look at three former basketball stars currently active at the collegiate level: Luke Barrett at St. Mary’s College, Luke Harris at Carleton College, and JoJo Murphy at Chico State. Luke Barrett St. Mary’s Luke Barrett, PHS Class of 2020, is a senior on the St. Mary’s basketball team appeared in 20 games last season. He helped lead Piedmont to its 2020 D4 North Coast Section title and won the Post’s Athlete of the Year award as a senior. The Gaels of St. Mary’s are off to a 2-3 start. Barrett has five appearances and is averaging 16 minutes per game. He has 14 points with four field goals and one 3-pointer, to go along with four assists and three steals. He’s been active on the boards with 22 rebounds, including 11 offensive grabs. St. Mary’s finished last season as the No. 22 ranked team in the country after going 27-8. They received the No. 5 seed in the NCAA Tournament, defeating No. 12 VCU 63-51 in the first round before losing 70-55 to UConn, the alma mater of Piedmont coach Ben Spencer. As a sophomore, Barrett made an appearance in the Gaels’ 82- 53 win over Indiana in the first round of the NCAA Tournament. Luke Harris Carleton College Luke Harris, PHS Class of 2021, is a junior at Carleton College in Minnesota and was also a member of Piedmont’s D4 NCS title in 2020. We named Harris the Post’s 2021 Athlete of the Year. The Knights won their first game of the season 57-50 over North Central Minnesota on November 15, led by Harris who tied a career-high with 26 points, to go along with three assists. As a sophomore, Harris helped lift Carleton to the Minnesota Intercollegiate Athletic Conference championship with a 86-76 win over St. Johns on February 26. Harris scored 19 points. He was second on the team in scoring with 16.4 points per game achieved double-digit points in 20 of 24 games last season, including eight games with at least 20 points. He led Carleton with 92 assists, was second on the team in field goals with 159 made, and was third in rebounds with 132. Carleton finished with a 24-4 overall record and lost 81-77 to St. Norbert in the first round of the Division 3 NCAA tournament. Harris departed from Piedmont High as an all-time great, finishing with over 1,200 points scored. He was a three-year starter in successful years, going 21-11 as a sophomore, won the 2020 D4 NCS Championship that finished 24-6, while the team went 11-5 in the pandemic shortened 2021 season. JoJo Murphy Chico State JoJo Murphy, PHS Class of 2022, is a sophomore at Chico State and was another member of Piedmont’s NCS title-winning team when he earned a starting role as a sophomore. The Wildcats are off to a hot 3-0 start to its season. Murphy has started all three games, scoring 35 points with 10 field goals and seven 3-pointers, including five steals and one assist. articles.text: St. Paul’s Episcopal Church in Oakland is delighted to welcome the community to a rare performance of the Choir of Clare College Cambridge in their only Bay Area performance. The internationally acclaimed choir will perform a Christmas concert, Magnum Mysterium, at 8 p.m. on Wednesday, December 13. Tickets are $40 General Admission, and $30 Seniors & Students, and are available in advance at https:// tinyurl.com/3j742ctz. Join us for an evening of festive melodies and harmonies at this highly anticipated event. The world-renowned Choir of Clare College, Cambridge, led by Graham Ross will perform for one night only at St. Paul’s Episcopal Church, 114 Montecito Avenue, across from Lake Merritt in Oakland. The choir’s holiday program includes the richness of Renaissance polyphony by Praetorius, Morales, and Mouton and masterpieces by Howells, Sally Beamish, Will Todd, along with favorites of the holiday season. The choir’s holiday program includes the richness of Renaissance music by Praetorius, Morales, and Mouton and masterpieces by Howells, Sally Beamish, Will Todd, along with favorites of the holiday season. Audiences will be thrilled by the virtuosity and rich sonorities of the group that British composer Giles Swayne refers to as “a whopping jewel in Clare’s musical crown.” Don’t miss the opportunity to experience the extraordinary talent of the Choir of Clare College in person in Oakland. For mer directors have included John Rutter and Timothy Brown. Under the direction of Graham Ross, Director of Music since 2010, it has been praised for its consistently ‘thrilling’ and ‘outstanding’ performances worldwide. Recent engagements include performances with the Orchestra of the Age of the Enlightenment, London Philharmonic Orchestra, Britten Sinfonia, Aalborg Symphony Orchestra on Denmark, Malaysian Philharmonic Orchestra in Kuala Lumpur, and Orquesta Sinfonia Nacional de Mexico. They have also performed in Barcelona’s Palau de Musica, El Escorial in Madrid, Palacio de Bellas Artes in Mexico City, St John’s Smith Square London, and across the USA and Canada. articles.text: Berkeley Repertory Theatre’s Bulrusher, a play by Eisa Davis and directed by Nicole Watson, will be performed on stage through Sunday, December 3. The coming-of-age story follows protagonist and titular character Bulrusher, a multiracial girl found as an infant floating in a basket on the Navarro River in Mendocino County. The girl, now 18-year-old, is clairvoyant, and struggles with feeling she is an outsider in the predominately white town of Boonville. The lyrical comedy takes a turn when the teenager meets a young Black woman from Birmingham, Alabama, who helps her uncover her past. The play deals with adults topics including sexual assault, but is grounded in humor and empathy. “Even though there’s a lot of pain and longing we’re left with, there’s also so much hope,” Davis told the Hollywood Reporter. “So that’s something that has kind of been sustaining for me in Bulrusher and a big part of why I wrote it – the possibility for love and forgiveness and joy, even amongst all of this pain.” The cast includes Cyndii Johnson, Rob Kellogg, Jamie LaVerdiere, Shyla Lefner, Jordan Tyson and Jeorge Bennett Watson. Bulrusher is directed by Nicole Watson. To purchase tickets, visit https://www.berkeleyrep.org/ shows/bulrusher/. articles.text: Review by Chris Honoré Paris Can Wait, directed by Eleanor Coppola, is easy on the eyes and the palate. Through a series of circumstances, Anne Lockwood (Diane Lane), wife of film producer Michael Lockwood (Alec Baldwin), decides, because of a slight ear infection, not to fly with him to Turkey and then on to Paris where they’ll spend some time vacationing. Michael’s French friend, Jaques (Arnaud Viard), insists that he will drive Anne across the South of France to Paris where she and Michael have an apartment waiting. And so what begins as a daylong road trip turns into a sightseeing buffet with countless stops at restaurants and a charming hotel. The scenery is gorgeous, the meals that she and Jaques share are amazing, and the table chit-chat is conversation lite. As Anne keeps suggesting/ insisting that Paris awaits, Jaques reminds her in countless ways that it’s not the destination but the journey. This trip is not only a life lesson for Anne but a metaphor. As it turns out, Paris does wait and Anne begins to relax. She carries a point and shoot camera and photographs not only the scenery but the stunning food that is served, meal after meal. This proves to be an interesting adjunct to the story, an affirmation of what is before her. Jaques is a raconteur, charming and light-hearted, and who at the drop of a broken fan belt will suggest a picnic before concerning himself with a repair. He is filled with a casual joie de vivre that slowly breaks down Anne’s defenses, though she is not so naïve to be taken in completely by his suave though sincere romantic banter. Diane Lane is, in my opinion, one of the best actors working today. Her face is a tableau of emotions; she easily inhabits any role she takes on. It is Lane who carries this film from their departure in Cannes in Jaques’ antique Peugeot to their arrival in Paris, eventually. As an aside, Eleanor Coppola is the wife of Francis Ford Coppola and this, at the age of 80, is her first feature. My sense is that it is subtly autobiographical. Paris Can Wait. articles.text: Madina Nalwanga in Queen of Katwe Queen of Katwe is a remarkable movie – moving, inspirational and yet possesses a frayed edge of reality that enhances the film. It is an example of the fine directorial work of Indian-American director, Mira Nair. There are two leading characters that fill the screen with a series of evocative and extraordinary moments. There’s Phiona Mutesi (Madina Nalwanga), child of the Kampala slum known as Katwe (Kampala is the capital of Uganda). And there is the slum itself, portrayed in all of its unforgiving, stark reality. Its genre is the Holocaust, a source for countless stories that ponder the existential question of how such a profound failure of the human spirit and conscience could ever have occurred? It is assumed that we have seen the horrifying images of men and women, mere skeletons, covered in striped rags, pressed against a wire fence, their hollow eyes gazing out, vacant and beyond reach. For that moment, at least, they have survived an abyss that still remains all but indescribable; yet, we know now, fully, that it did occur and some of those who stood at the wire or lay crowded in wooden slatted bunks have born witness to a barbarity the description of which still eludes even those who lived it. In the course of our lives it may be that we have grown inured to those images: human beings stacked like cords of wood, awaiting their final journey into deep pits or ovens. But Hungarian writer and director Laszlo Nemes has created in Son of Saul a film that avoids the standard Holocaust tropes: the camera panning a concentration camp (in this case its Auschwitz-Birkenau), shots of Nazi guards patrolling the perimeters with snarling dogs, or barracks with smoke stacks in the background. Instead, he focuses on one man, Saul (Geza Rohrig), and using a shallow focus format and an almost square screen, he follows him closely, intently. pages.text: Wednesday, November 22, 2023 19 MOVIE FOR ADULTS Paris Can Wait an enjoyable romantic comedy Review by Chris Honoré Paris Can Wait, directed by Eleanor Coppola, is easy on the eyes and the palate. Through a series of circumstances, Anne Lockwood (Diane Lane), wife of film producer Michael Lockwood (Alec Baldwin), decides, because of a slight ear infection, not to fly with him to Turkey and then on to Paris where they’ll spend some time vacationing. Michael’s French friend, Jaques (Arnaud Viard), insists that he will drive Anne across the South of France to Paris where she and Michael have an apartment waiting. And so what begins as a daylong road trip turns into a sightseeing buffet with countless stops at restaurants and a charming hotel. The scenery is gorgeous, the meals that she and Jaques share are amazing, and the table chit-chat is conversation lite. As Anne keeps suggesting/ insisting that Paris awaits, Jaques reminds her in countless ways that it’s not the destination but the journey. This trip is not only a life lesson for Anne but a metaphor. As it turns out, Paris does wait and Anne begins to relax. She carries a point and shoot camera and photographs not only the scenery but the stunning food that is served, meal after meal. This proves to be an interesting adjunct to the story, an affirmation of what is before her. Jaques is a raconteur, charming and light-hearted, and who at the drop of a broken fan belt will suggest a picnic before concerning himself with a repair. He is filled with a casual joie de vivre that slowly breaks down Anne’s defenses, though she is not so naïve to be taken in completely by his suave though sincere romantic banter. Diane Lane is, in my opinion, one of the best actors working today. Her face is a tableau of emotions; she easily inhabits any role she takes on. It is Lane who carries this film from their departure in Cannes in Jaques’ antique Peugeot to their arrival in Paris, eventually. As an aside, Eleanor Coppola is the wife of Francis Ford Coppola and this, at the age of 80, is her first feature. My sense is that it is subtly autobiographical. Paris Can Wait. articles.text: Zoo’s famous lantern festival, Glowfari, now open The Oakland Zoo’s annual Glowfari adventure has begun. Oakland Zoo has opened its gates to nighttime visitors for Glowfari, its wildly popular illuminated lantern festival. Glowfari features hundreds of new, largerthan-life animal lanterns that will enchant guests of all ages. The experience of walking through the rows of glowing lanterns gives off a feeling of Disneyland’s Main Street Electric Parade. Each lantern tells part of the journey of wildlife, the importance of every species on the planet, and Oakland Zoo’s commitment to conservation. This year’s display features themes of the forests of North America with native wildlife, notably mountain lions and wolves. Lanterns also help draw attention to the Arctic, the Deep Ocean and animals of the Bayou. Guests can finish their nocturnal visit by riding on the Zoo’s train through the great red island of Madagascar, a wondrous world full of lemurs and chameleons. The winter wonderland also includes a visit from Santa who will be stationed (weather permitting) in the Rides Area from Friday to Sunday in November and every night in December to the 23rd from 6:00-8:45 p.m. Glowfari will continue in January on select days from 5:00- 9:00 p.m. Oakland Zoo will be open this month from November 18-22, 24-26, and 29-30. Oakland Zoo is located at 9777 Golf Links Rd in Oakland. Call 632-9525 for more information, or click on Oaklandzoo.org. A guest a Glowfari inspects a life-size polar bear lantern. Signs in the zoo help teach guests about each species and animal conservation efforts. ®

articles.text: Balancing festive cheer and healthy living As the holiday season approaches, many of us look forward to festive gatherings, delicious meals, and sweet treats. However, the fear of the notorious 8-lb. holiday weight gain can often cast a shadow over the joyous celebrations. The good news is that you can enjoy the holidays to the fullest without sacrificing your health and fitness. Here’s how to strike the right balance and savor the season guilt-free. One of the keys to avoiding holiday weight gain is practicing mindful indulgence. Rather than restricting yourself, allow yourself to enjoy your favorite holiday treats in moderation. Eat slowly, savor each bite, and listen to your body’s signals of fullness. By being mindful of your eating habits, you can avoid overindulging while still relishing the festive Don’t let the holiday hustle and bustle disrupt your regular exercise routine. Whether it’s a brisk walk after a hearty meal, a quick home workout, or a festive dance party, staying active can help counteract the effects of indulgent holiday feasts. Aim for at least 30 minutes of moderate exercise most days of the week to keep your metabolism active and your energy levels high. Be sure to include family or friends for a nice walk. 3. Hydrate, Hydrate, Hydrate Often overlooked during the holiday season, staying hydrated is crucial for overall well-being. Sometimes, our bodies confuse thirst with hunger, leading to unnecessary snacking. Ensure you drink plenty of water throughout the day to stay hydrated and minimize the chances of overeating. 4. Choose Healthier Alternatives Get creative in the kitchen by incorporating healthier alternatives into your holiday meals. Experiment with lighter versions of your favorite recipes, substitute ingredients with healthier options, and focus on nutrient-dense foods. You can still enjoy delicious meals without compromising on taste or your waistline. 5. Prioritize Sleep A well-rested body is better equipped to handle the demands of the holiday season. Aim for 7-9 hours of quality sleep each night to support your overall health. A good night’s sleep can also help regulate your appetite and reduce the likelihood of mindless snacking. Minimize alcohol consumption as it can disrupt REM sleep. 6. Socialize and Move Instead of solely focusing on food during holiday gatherings, prioritize socializing and engaging in activities with friends and family. Plan active outings, organize games, or take a post-meal stroll together. By incorporating movement into your celebrations, you’ll not only burn calories but also create lasting memories. 7. Set Realistic Goals Rather than aiming for perfection, set realistic and achievable health goals for the holiday season. This could include maintaining your current weight, staying active, or trying a new fitness routine. Having clear, attainable goals will help you stay focused and motivated. articles.text: Early Monday morning, November 13, a residential burglary occurred at a house under construction on the 200 block of Greenbank Avenue. The suspects gained access to the rear of the house and forced their way in through the backdoor. The homeowner returned to the residence that morning to find several large items missing, including a new Samsung kitchen range, new TOTObrand toilet, miscellaneous tools, a paintball gun with the victim’s name etched onto it, and a Huusk brand knife. The loss was valued at $5,500 and damage to the residence of $6,000. Surveillance video from a neighbor showed that suspects used a white 2018 Ford F150 without a license plate. By using the city’s Automatic License Plate Readers (ALPR), PPD officers were able to find the car’s license plate, and a records check revealed the car was registered to an address on Harrison Street in Oakland. Piedmont police observed the Ford pickup in the driveway at the Harrison Street address. A Samsung kitchen range was in the truck bed. The officer waited until the truck’s owners returned and then conducted an investigative stop, identifying the driver and passenger as Jose Lopez Escobar and Christian Briseno respectively. A search of Briseno revealed narcotics and narcotics equipment. Both occupants of the vehicle were detained, and a search of the Ford revealed stolen property in addition to three replica firearms and burglary tools. Both suspects were placed under arrest for burglary and possession of stolen property. Lopez Escobar was booked into Santa Rita Jail for burglary, possession of stolen property, possession of burglary tools, and driving with a suspended license. Briseno was booked into Santa Rita Jail for burglary, possession of stolen property, possession of drug paraphernalia, possession of meth, and an outstanding warrant. Piedmont Police Capt. Chris Monahan said that this arrest would not have been possible without the department’s ALPR cameras. “We did not have the plate of the truck from the neighbor’s residential video. The suspect’s vehicle was located in the ALPR system, which did have the plate, which ultimately led to their arrest,” said Monahan. articles.text: Piedmont Police received an automated license plate reader notification at 4:16 a.m. on Wednesday, November 15, for a stolen black Kia Sedona entering the city on Somerset Road. The vehicle was reported as stolen three days earlier from Cambridge Way in Piedmont. Officers located the vehicle minutes later on Somerset, but the driver of the Kia intentionally struck two patrol cars in an attempt to escape. One unoccupied patrol vehicle was pushed down Somerset before becoming lodged on the side of the roadway. Officers responded on foot and took both occupants of the Kia into custody. A search of the driver, Oscar Garcia, 36 years old from San Leandro, and the vehicle revealed burglary tools, narcotics, and stolen credit cards. The driver was arrested, and booked into Santa Rita Jail for assault with a deadly weapon, resisting police, vandalism, evading, possession of a stolen car, possession of stolen property, burglary tools and narcotics. A records check of the passenger, Diana Martinez Valencia, 36, showed that she was on a pretrial release with a full search clause. A search found narcotics and she was booked into Santa Rita Jail for failing to follow a court order and narcotics possession.
